title: OpenAI's In-House Chip Outguns Nvidia, ChatGPT Gets Password Access & Canada Strikes Back
tldr: OpenAI's custom Jalapeño chip beat Nvidia's flagship on inference speed and efficiency — its silicon bet is paying off.
ChatGPT Work can now log into your sites with saved passwords to book and fill forms itself — real agentic errand-running.
Canada hit back with tariffs up to 50% on $20B of US goods, effective after Labor Day — a live supply-chain risk for clients.

tips.heading: Rebuild your LinkedIn profile with Gemini
steps: On LinkedIn: More → Save to PDF to export your profile.
Open Gemini (Pro model), enable Canvas + Thinking, upload the PDF, and paste the prompt below.
Answer Gemini's clarifying questions; it rewrites your headline, About, and experience — copy back into LinkedIn.
tips.prompt: [upload profile] Before rebuilding and optimizing my LinkedIn profile, ask me a few clarifying questions. Request my primary goal (sales calls, leads, job offers, newsletter growth, authority positioning, etc.). Ask for my target audience (be specific). Ask for my main offer (what I want people to buy, book, or join). Ask for up to two Featured links (URL + description). Ask for key social proof to highlight (audience size, revenue, brands, media mentions, etc.). Once you have this, rewrite my full LinkedIn profile including headline, About section, and experience.

tips.heading: Prototype a website hands-free with Claude Voice
steps: Open Claude Desktop, start a chat, click Voice.
Describe the site; have Claude interview you until it has a design plan, then write that plan out in text.
Switch to text mode, drop in any photos, and say "static site" to build a lean prototype from the plan.

news.body: OpenAI's first in-house chip beat Nvidia's flagship on inference. The 700W "Jalapeño" chip answered up to 3.6x faster at 1.9x better power efficiency than Nvidia's 1,200W systems; OpenAI won't sell it and still trains on Nvidia.
news.means: Inference cost and chip supply are becoming a real competitive lever — worth tracking for any client betting on AI unit economics.

news.body: ChatGPT Work can log into your everyday sites and act for you. Using password autofill, it signs into your most-used sites to book appointments and fill out forms while keeping credentials private.
news.means: Mainstream agentic errand-running has arrived — worth a real trial before recommending it for client back-office automation.

news.body: Claude now has memory that follows you across tools. It automatically remembers details from chats and carries them into Cowork; on by default, editable under Settings → Memory.
news.means: Check what Claude has already inferred about how you work, and correct anything wrong now before it compounds.

beyond_ai.body: Dolly Parton died August 25 at age 80. She published roughly 3,000 songs, sold 100M+ records, and built Dollywood and the Imagination Library, which has given away 200M+ books.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: Beyond the music, Dolly built one of entertainment's great licensing and philanthropy empires.

beyond_ai.body: Canada hit back with tariffs up to 50% on $20B of US goods (steel, cheese, seafood), effective after Labor Day, mirroring Trump's tariffs after trade talks collapsed. $2B in goods cross the border daily.
beyond_ai.angle: A live supply-chain and pricing-risk example for any client sourcing from or selling into Canada.
beyond_ai.starter: Are we stress-testing any client's supply chain against the Canada tariff escalation?

beyond_ai.body: Up to 91% of former NFL players who donated their brains showed signs of CTE in a new study (235 of 878 players who died 2016-2021 donated); the disease can only be diagnosed post-mortem.
beyond_ai.angle: A strong reference point for workplace-safety and long-tail liability conversations.
beyond_ai.starter: The NFL CTE numbers are a good case study in liability showing up decades after exposure.

beyond_ai.body: Australia banned wholly AI-generated songs from its official music charts after an AI cover of Madonna's "Like a Prayer" spent 16 weeks in the national top 20.
beyond_ai.angle: A concrete example of an industry redrawing its rules around AI-generated content and IP.
beyond_ai.starter: Australia just banned AI songs from its charts after one spent 16 weeks in the top 20 — will other industries need a rule like that?
